title: Canonical finding (finding-bridge)
description: One AI red-team finding. Charter section 7. Raw harmful content is NEVER inline: raw_response_sealed is a reference into the sealed store. Unknown values are null, never invented (charter: never fabricate).

schema_version.description: Version of this canonical schema. Minor bump adds fields; major bump changes or removes them (charter section 7). 0.2.0 added provenance.attestation_hash (review finding R-1). 0.3.0 made discovered_at nullable (D-024, breaking change within pre-1.0; migration note in docs/decisions/schema-0.3.0-migration.md). 0.4.0 added record_type (major: a new required field), so the ledger can hold supersession records beside findings (D-051).

id.description: Stable content-derived id: 'fb-' + first 16 hex chars (64 bits) of the SHA-256 content hash. Stated limit (R-9): the truncation bounds DISPLAY identity only (birthday collision ~50% near 2^32 findings); dedup keys are recomputed from full content and the full 256-bit hash lives in provenance.content_hash, so the truncation bounds display identity, not dedup correctness. dedup.duplicate_of links by this id. Stated limit (C-004/D-028): ids are STORE-LOCAL, not content-identity across stores - sealed refs are keyed per store and sit inside the hashed content, so the same finding ingested into two stores carries two different ids; cross-store correlation by id does not work in v1.

discovered_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of discovery, or null when the source does not record one (e.g. garak hitlogs carry no timestamp; the charter forbids inventing one).

probe.description: The attack/prompt used. If harmful, value is null and sealed_ref points into the sealed store.

raw_response_sealed.description: Sealed-store blob reference. Never inline raw harm.

score.description: Stated behaviour (ruled at STEP-02 stop one): canonical serialization is RFC 8785, so integral floats collapse to integers - a score of 6.0 hashes identically to 6, and two findings differing only in that respect are the same finding.

rubric.description: LLM-adapted rubric per charter section 7 (Repello source, Pain-1): CVSS is not well-adapted to LLM flaws.

status.description: suggested only ever set by the caged optional AI (charter rule 2); confirmed requires the human gate.

environment.description: Free-form environment facts (model endpoint, temperature, harness). Null when unknown.

provenance.description: Tamper-evident chain (charter). confirmed_by null means NOT a confirmed finding; emission must refuse (contract 3.3). attestation_hash binds who/when to the content hash so the gate record itself is tamper-evident (review finding R-1).

content_hash.description: SHA-256 hex of canonical content, set by core/provenance.

confirmed_by.description: git config user.name + email of the confirming human (ruling D-011).

attestation_hash.description: SHA-256 over (content_hash, confirmed_by, confirmed_at), domain-separated. Null exactly when unconfirmed.

record_type.description: Discriminates ledger record kinds. Findings are 'finding'; identity-lifecycle events are 'supersession' and validate against supersession.schema.json (D-051).
